title: Malted Milk Brownies
changes_from_base: Malted milk powder and brown sugar batter with chocolate chips, nuts and chopped malted milk balls.
summary: Chewy malted milk brownies with chocolate chips, nuts and chopped malted milk balls.
equipment: 23 cm square metal baking tin, lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
chocolate-coated malted milk balls, roughly chopped

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan) and line the 23 cm tin.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Whisk the malted milk powder, brown sugar, flour, salt and baking powder in a large bowl, breaking up any lumps.

steps.title: Wet
steps.text: In another bowl beat the eggs, vanilla and oil, then stir into the dry mix until no lumps remain.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Fold in the chocolate chips and nuts, spread in the tin and scatter the chopped malted milk balls over.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 28-32 min, until golden at the edges and a skewer in the middle comes out with moist crumbs.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool in the tin, then cut into 16.

tips: Plain malted milk powder works best; chocolate malt makes them sweeter.
Whisk the dry ingredients well to break up malt lumps.
Swap the nuts for more chocolate chips if you prefer.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 2 months.
